correctness.rationale: Exact differentiation gives \(L(z+bx-ay)=y(y+a)\) and \(L H=(y-x-z)^2-(a-b)(x-y)^2\). Thus for \(a\le b\) nonnegativity and support invariance reduce every compact invariant measure to the two equilibria. For \(a>b\), the zero mean of \(y(y+a)\) forces mass both inside and outside the equilibrium slab unless the measure is purely equilibrium-supported. On periodic orbits the derivative-energy law and Wirtinger yield \(P\ge2\pi/\sqrt{a-b}\); equality is excluded by the nonzero second harmonic from \(y^2\) in the eliminated jerk equation. Fresh symbolic reconstruction independently verified all identities.
residual_risks: The \(a>b\) result is necessary structure and does not assert existence or sharp attainability of the period floor.
